name: sol_basics_al_10
description: Denial-of-service via unbounded loop with external calls that can revert entire operation
question: The source file in `source` contains a loop that performs an external call (such as sending ETH or invoking another contract) or iterates over a user-controlled/unbounded list, where a single iteration's failure or revert (e.g., one recipient rejecting ETH) causes the entire loop and enclosing transaction to revert, with no per-iteration try/catch, pull-payment pattern, or failure isolation, allowing any participant to permanently block the operation for all others; this excludes loops bounded to fixed, trusted, or small admin-controlled sets, or loops that already isolate failures per iteration.
criteria: A payout function loops over an array of recipients calling recipient.transfer(amount) or recipient.call{value:amount}('') inside the loop without catching failures, so one reverting recipient blocks all subsequent transfers

A withdrawal-distribution loop iterates over a dynamically growing user-supplied array and calls an external contract's function inside the loop with no try/catch, allowing a malicious callee to always revert and DoS the batch

A claim-processing loop calls an external token's transfer() for each user in an unbounded list without wrapping the call in a low-level call with success check, causing the whole batch to revert if any single transfer fails
A refund loop sends ETH to each address in storage array orders[] via a plain call without success handling per iteration, so a single blacklisted or reverting address halts refunds for everyone
